subject: SLA: aggregated monthly credit & latency graceband discussion
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@polarishealth.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@polarishealth.com, john.cartwright@polarishealth.com
Date: 2027-05-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: SLA template — monthly credit aggregation idea

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement reviewed Redwood's standard SLA and we have two related asks before we can move to signatures:

1) We operate across three regions and would prefer credits to be aggregated across the account each month (one consolidated remedy) rather than per-region line items. That helps our finance team avoid multiple small reimbursements.
2) For latency, our production load includes periodic batch inference (2–3 scheduled jobs/day) that temporarily increases 95th percentile latency for a few minutes. We want a carveout or a small "graceband" so we aren't credited for tiny, predictable spikes caused by scheduled batch windows.

Can you confirm if Redwood can:
- Offer a single monthly credit calculation that sums availability/latency shortfalls across regions and issues one credit payment?
- Define a latency "graceband" (for example, ignore latency degradations shorter than X minutes or below Y% of total tokens) or propose an alternative operational carveout?

I've attached our procurement checklist and a short spreadsheet with sample monthly rollups to show what consolidated credits would look like on our side.

Maya

[Attachment: polaris-procurement-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)]
[Attachment: polaris-monthly-rollup-example.csv (text/csv)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@polarishealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-08T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: SLA template — monthly credit aggregation idea

Hi Maya — really appreciate the clear ask and the sample rollup.

Short answer: yes, we're open to an aggregated monthly remedy and to defining a graceband for predictable batch windows; we just need to pin operational definitions so there's no ambiguity during post-incident reconciliation. Proposed approach below (attachment: redwood-sla-proposal-2027-05-08.pdf):

1) Aggregated monthly credit:
- We calculate credits per-region as usual, then sum credits for the account at the end of the billing month and issue a single consolidated credit line item on the invoice.
- Minimum threshold: to avoid trivial micro-credits, credits under $50/month will be rounded and held until they exceed $50 or until customer requests payout.

2) Batch window graceband (latency carveout):
- Customers may declare up to 6 scheduled batch windows per region per month (each window up to 30 minutes). Any degradations that fall completely within these declared windows are excluded from latency credit calculations.
- For unscheduled but short-lived spikes, we propose a "short-duration forgiveness" rule: single latency excursions under 5 minutes that affect less than 2% of total requests in the window are excluded.

Operational notes:
- We need a signed schedule of recurring batch windows (time zone + pattern) for each region in the initial SOW. Ad-hoc changes can be submitted via support and will be considered for the following month.
- All rollups and calculations will be visible in the Redwood Console (per-month remediation worksheet).

I'll loop in Laura (ops) and Aditya (contracts) to confirm the implementation and legal wording. If that direction looks acceptable, we can update the SLA draft and push a DocuSign.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
[karthik.iyer@redwood.com]

[Attachment: redwood-sla-proposal-2027-05-08.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@polarishealth.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-09T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: SLA template — monthly credit aggregation idea

Thanks Maya/Karthik — operational confirmation from our side below. A few clarifying points so the carveout can't be misinterpreted in production: 

- Declarations: the scheduled batch windows must be mutually agreed and recorded in the SOW appendix A. If Polaris runs dynamic batch windows without prior notice and we detect misuse, we reserve the right to exclude those windows from credit calculations.
- Observability: to apply the short-duration forgiveness rule we need token-level request attribution (which we have for Polaris under your onboarding config). The rule won't apply if request attribution is incomplete.
- Transparency: we'll include a monthly "credit rollup" CSV in the invoice packet showing per-region calculations, items excluded due to graceband, and the final consolidated credit amount.

Operational workaround suggestion (to reduce complexity): for customers with a predictable batch pattern we can offer a small monthly fixed "batch allowance" (e.g., 0.1% uptime buffer) in lieu of declaring windows. That may be easier for finance teams that don't want to manage a schedule. We can flag that option in the SOW as an alternate path.

If this looks good to you, Aditya can draft the legal language for the SOW appendix and the DocuSign envelope.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Platform Operations
[laura.bennett@redwood.com]

From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@polarishealth.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@polarishealth.com, john.cartwright@polarishealth.com
Date: 2027-05-10T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: SLA template — monthly credit aggregation idea

Karthik/Laura — thank you, this is very helpful and aligns with what our finance team wanted. A couple quick confirmations: 

- Aggregated monthly credit + $50 micro-credit hold is acceptable.
- We will declare up to 3 scheduled batch windows per region initially (we'll list them in appendix A) and reserve the option to move to the fixed monthly "batch allowance" if the schedule becomes onerous.
- Please add the short-duration forgiveness rule (5 minutes / 2% threshold) into the SOW language; we'll accept the observability caveat.

Next step for us: procurement will review your updated SLA draft and DocuSign. Can you send the DocuSign link once Aditya has added the appendix language? Our target is to sign by end of month.

Thanks,
Maya Singh
Senior Procurement Manager, Polaris Health
